Treatment summary
Pateint presented following a low-speed collision in a parking lot with complaints of neck pain, stiffness, and headache consistent
with cervical strain. Over the course of 29 visits, care consisted of conservative management including manual therapy,
supervised therapeutic exercise, and home execrise instruction. Treatment progressed along a typical recovery pattern, with visit
frequency decreasing as symptoms improved and range of motion increased. Examination revealed reduced cervical range of
motion and paraspinal tenderness that support the reported injury, while neurological screening, reflexes, and strength testing
remained within normal limits. The mechanism of injury is reasonably consistent with the reported symptoms. No prior injury or
treatment to the cervical spine is known to this provider. Billing records reflect single, appropriately spaced charges for each
service rendered, with no duplicate entries. At discharge, the patient was improving and was advised to continue independent
home exercise as needed.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

- "reason": one short sentence.
